informal.text: Construct finite magmas of every positive size satisfying law 1482: x = (y ◇ x) ◇ (x ◇ (y ◇ y)), using the paper's mostly-constant model construction.
informal.scope: Only the explicit all-finite-sizes model construction for law 1482; no claim of 3074-law classification, closure coverage, dual laws, or classification completeness. This is a size-uniform construction subproject, not an individual implication exercise.

source_locators.text: These considerations account for $\num{3068}$ laws, and there remain three dual pairs of laws to treat.  This is done through ad hoc models: a piecewise linear model for $\Eq{1682}$ and its dual, and models whose operation table is mostly constant for the remaining laws $\Eq{1482}$, $\Eq{1523}$, and their duals.

source_locators.text:
Since a law implied by a full spectrum law has full spectrum itself, the implication graph reduces significantly the number of laws for which it is useful to formalize the full spectrum property.  Accounting for duality and implications, we found it sufficient to formalize the proof that $32$ laws have no magma of size~$2$ or none of size~$3$, and the explicit construction of magmas of all finite sizes for the $7$~laws $\Eq{4}$, $\Eq{41}$, $\Eq{492}$, $\Eq{543}$, $\Eq{1482}$, $\Eq{1523}$, and $\Eq{1682}$.  In conclusion, we prove that $
um{3074}$ laws ($65\%$) have full spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}(\Eq{n})=\mathbb{Z}_{>0}$ and $
um{1620}$ ($35\%$) do not (including $
um{1496}$ laws equivalent to $\Eq{2}$).  These percentages remain roughly stable at higher orders, with $60\%$ of laws of order up to $9$ having full spectrum, as will be reported elsewhere.
source_locators.selected_target: explicit construction of magmas of all finite sizes for law 1482 in the seven-law list
